It is submitted that the advice of the Commission to “henceforth” approach the Central Government came subsequently only in the order dated 31.1.2025 in Petition No. 365/AT/2024 and as on the date of issuance of RfS in the present case i.e., on 8.11.2024, there was no direction or finding of the Commission for seeking an approval for deviations from the Hybrid Guidelines from the Central Government instead of the State Government. Accordingly, the treatment of Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 5.11.2024 passed by the Commission in Petition No. 365/AT/2024 as a directive constitutes an error apparent and warrants a review/correction of the impugned order. 5. We have considered the submissions advanced by the Review Petitioner. However, prior to dealing with the above submissions, it would be pertinent to refer to the relevant extract of the impugned order: _2_ **_. In response to the specific query of the Commission regarding any deviations in the Bid documents and the prior approval thereof, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner had undertaken certain deviations in the Bid documents from the provisions of the Solar Guidelines and for such deviations, it has obtained the approval of Government of West Bengal._** _5. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission ordered as under:_ 6. The primary argument of the Review Petitioner is that in the paragraph 33 of the impugned order, the Commission while observing that the Review Petitioner was well aware on 5.11.2024 of the wrong so committed by it, viz. taking the approval on the deviation(s) from the provisions of the Hybrid Guidelines from the Government of West Bengal instead of the Central Government has treated its Record of Proceedings for hearing dated 5.11.2024 in Petition No. 365/MP/2024 as a directive, whereas, by said Record of Proceedings, the Commission had only raised a query therein seeking an explanation from the Review Petitioner. However, we find this argument misconceived for the reason that nowhere does the impugned order treat the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 5.11.2024, passed in Petition No. 365/AT/2024 a directive upon the Review Petitioner. Paragraph 32 of the impugned order clearly records that by the said Record of Proceedings, the Petitioner was directed to explain how the Appropriate Government, as envisaged in Clause 16 of the Solar Guidelines, would be a State Government since the case therein involved an inter-State supply of electricity. The said explanation was called for in view of the position laid down by the Hon’ble **_80],_** which explained the meaning of expressions Appropriate Government and Appropriate Commission under the Act in respect of the inter-State transactions. All that the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 5.11.2024 did was put to the notice of the Review Petitioner the prevailing position in law while seeking its explanation thereon. 7. Furthermore, bare reading of the subsequent paragraphs of the impugned order, particularly the paragraphs 34 to 36, clearly reveals that the observation at paragraph 33 of the impugned order that the Petitioner was well aware on 5.11.2024 of wrong so committed by it is not on the basis of the treating the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 5.11.2024 issued in Petition No. 365/AT/2024 as a directive. These paragraphs note that the meaning of the expressions Appropriate Government and Appropriate Commission under the Act, in respect of inter-State transactions, came to be explained by the Energy Watchdog Judgment way back in 2017 and by the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 5.11.2024. The Review Petitioner was also made aware of the above position. Paragraph 36 of the impugned order also reflects on this and specifically notes that pursuant to the Commission’s observation dated 5.11.2024 in Petition No. 365/AT/2024, the Review Petitioner ought to have taken suitable measures in respect of the subsequent RfS as issued on 8.11.2024. In our view, the absence of any specific direction in the said Record of Proceedings requiring the Review Petitioner to approach the Central Government instead of the State Government did not excuse the Review Petitioner for not following the prevailing position of law despite being made aware of it.
